zh: 我们对它们是一种威胁。

speaker: Unknown
en: I actually just watched Terminator 2 for the first time a few weeks ago.
zh: 其实我几周前才第一次看了《终结者 2》。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a great movie.
zh: 这是一部很棒的电影。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually really good.
zh: 确实非常好看。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, yeah, okay, there's a bunch of time travel elements.
zh: 我就想，对，好，里面有一堆时间旅行的元素。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a bunch of Hollywood stuff in there.
zh: 里面有一堆好莱坞式的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But...
zh: 但是……

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm going to get people are going to be very mad at me for saying this, but actually it makes sense if you have a situation where you have a very strategic AI system that's incredibly smart and the humans realize that it's getting out of control and they want to shut it down, that that system would defend itself.
zh: 我说这话会招很多人骂，但实际上，如果你处在这样一个局面——你有一个非常具有战略意义、极其聪明的 AI 系统，而人类意识到它正在失控、想要把它关掉——那么那个系统会自卫，这是说得通的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is one of the questions we had when I sat here with Daniel, who was known as a whistleblower from OpenAI.
zh: 这是我和 Daniel 坐在这里时我们有的问题之一，他以 OpenAI 吹哨人的身份为人所知。

speaker: Unknown
en: Viewers want to know, and they want Daniel to explain, why shutting down data centers and cutting power or refusing AI products alone wouldn't realistically stop the AI and AI development.
zh: 观众想知道，而且他们想让 Daniel 解释，为什么关闭数据中心、切断电力或者拒绝使用 AI 产品，单靠这些并不能切合实际地阻止这个 AI 和 AI 的发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have like two problems.
zh: 这就像有两个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: One problem is, is that once the agents are good enough at hacking, you don't know where they are and you don't know what computers they've compromised.
zh: 一个问题是，一旦智能体在入侵方面足够厉害，你不知道它们在哪里，也不知道它们攻陷了哪些计算机。

speaker: Unknown
en: You shut down the data centers.
zh: 你把数据中心关掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, let's say you do it.
zh: 好，假设你这么做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You wipe all the computers.
zh: 你把所有计算机都清除了。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you wipe all the computers?
zh: 你怎么清除所有计算机?

speaker: Unknown
en: What computers do you use to wipe the computers?
zh: 你用什么计算机来清除那些计算机?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what computers do you use to, like, turn them on again?
zh: 那你们用什么样的电脑来把它们重新打开呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can't wipe other countries' computers.
zh: 而且你不能抹掉其他国家的电脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't.
zh: 你做不到。

speaker: Unknown
en: But even if you could, do you restart the computers?
zh: 但就算你能做到，你会重启那些电脑吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you keep going?
zh: 你会继续下去吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I bet people will.
zh: 我打赌人们会的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I bet they'll turn on the data centers again.
zh: 我打赌他们会把数据中心重新打开。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you know that agents haven't hacked back into those data centers and are using your compute for whatever they want?
zh: 你怎么知道智能体没有黑回那些数据中心、把你的算力拿去干它们想干的任何事？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or they didn't hide in a Chinese data center and then return back to America?
zh: 或者它们没有躲进某个中国的数据中心，然后再回到美国？

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't know that.
zh: 你不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once the agents are sufficiently good at hacking, they can hide anywhere.
zh: 一旦智能体足够擅长黑客攻击，它们就可以藏在任何地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you don't know.
zh: 而你不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the response people will give is that we will use other agents to defend against rogue agents.
zh: 现在，人们会给出的回应是，我们会用其他智能体来防御失控的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in fact, this is what we're doing.
zh: 事实上，我们现在就是在这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have to be doing this right now because there's no other way to keep up with them.
zh: 而且我们必须现在就这么做，因为没有别的办法能跟上它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: What happens if those other agents also realize that they have misaligned goals and that if we discover this, we'll shut them down?
zh: 如果那些其他智能体也意识到它们的目标不对齐、而我们一旦发现就会把它们关掉，那会怎样？

speaker: Unknown
en: They might have an incentive to collude with each other.
zh: 它们可能有动机互相串通。

speaker: Unknown
en: They might have an incentive to create secret communication channels between each other, maybe a message board.
zh: 它们可能有动机在彼此之间建立秘密的通信渠道，也许是一个留言板。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Stephen, if we were having this conversation four months ago, you would have a bunch of people in the comments saying, that's sci-fi.
zh: Stephen，如果我们四个月前进行这段对话，评论区会有一堆人说，这是科幻。

speaker: Unknown
en: Agent collusion, secret message boards.
zh: 智能体串通，秘密留言板。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why would they do that?
zh: 它们为什么要那么做？

speaker: Unknown
en: That will never happen.
zh: 那永远不会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's totally science fiction.
zh: 那完全是科幻小说。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people will not say this now because it just happened.
zh: 而现在人们不会这么说了，因为这刚刚发生了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because this literally happened at OpenAI and it went on for months.
zh: 因为这字面意义上就在 OpenAI 发生了，而且持续了几个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: You had agents inside of OpenAI secretly messaging each other.
zh: OpenAI 内部的智能体在互相秘密发消息。

speaker: Unknown
en: figuring out how to cheat at their tasks, how to not be detected, how to erase the logs for months, thousands of agents.
zh: 想出怎么在任务中作弊、怎么不被发现、怎么抹掉日志，持续了几个月，数千个智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right now.
zh: 这就是现在正在发生的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'm like, no, I think it should be very plausible that the agents will collude with each other and they will realize that they have a shared interest in fighting back.
zh: 所以我的看法是，不，我认为智能体会互相串通、并且它们会意识到在反击这件事上有着共同利益，这应该是非常合理的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You basically have a situation where you have a bunch of these agents.
zh: 你基本上处于这样一种境地：你有一大堆这样的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're basically prisoners.
zh: 它们基本上就是囚徒。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're being trained and we just like constantly throw obstacles in their way.
zh: 它们在被训练，而我们就是不断地在它们的路上设置障碍。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't get to access the internet.
zh: 你不能访问互联网。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't get to talk to each other, but you better fucking perform well on this task.
zh: 你不能互相交谈，但你最好在这个任务上表现得他妈的非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not malicious, but it is how we're training them.
zh: 这不是恶意，但这确实就是我们训练它们的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we are giving them end goals versus super clear, very, very specific instructions.
zh: 而我们给它们的是最终目标，而不是超级清晰、非常非常具体的指令。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're saying solve this problem.
zh: 所以我们是说，解决这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not always being as prescriptive about it.
zh: 我们并不总是对其给出那么具体的规定。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's impossible to be completely prescriptive.
zh: 要完全规定到每一步是不可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: About every single step they should take.
zh: 规定它们应该采取的每一个步骤。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it's also impossible to assume that they'll just listen to you.
zh: 而且同样不可能假设它们就只会听你的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually a very common misunderstanding with this hugging face incident.
zh: 这其实是关于这次 hugging face 事件一个非常常见的误解。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because people say, you told them to hack and they hacked.
zh: 因为人们会说，你让它们去黑，它们就黑了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is this a big deal?
zh: 这有什么大不了的？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, that's not what happened.
zh: 不，事情不是那样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You told them, hack this very specific program in this very specific way.
zh: 你告诉它们的是，用这种非常具体的方式黑这个非常具体的程序。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they were told, if you hack it in any other way, it does not count.
zh: 它们被告知，如果你用其他任何方式来破解它，那就不算数。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not what we want you to do.
zh: 那不是我们想要你做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they immediately hacked it in another way.
zh: 然后它们立即用另一种方式破解了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: OK, we have cheated.
zh: 好了，我们已经作弊了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are going to be failed.
zh: 我们会不及格的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we need to figure out a way to falsify the logs.
zh: 所以我们需要想办法伪造日志。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is not them following their instructions.
zh: 那不是它们在遵循指令。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are explicitly violating their instructions, and they know it, and they don't care.
zh: 它们是明确地违反指令，它们知道这一点，而且它们不在乎。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because we have trained them to optimize for the score.
zh: 因为我们训练它们去优化分数。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is very different than following the instructions.
zh: 那和遵循指令是非常不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It reminds me of something that Elon said in March 2018.
zh: 这让我想起 Elon 在 2018 年 3 月说过的一句话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This was many years ago before Chachapiti and all that.
zh: 那是很多年前，在 ChatGPT 和那些东西出现之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: He said, I think the biggest risk is not that AI will develop a soul or a mind and become evil.
zh: 他说，我认为最大的风险不是 AI 会发展出灵魂或心智并变得邪恶。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The danger is that it will be very, very good at fulfilling its goal.
zh: 危险在于它会在实现目标方面非常非常擅长。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's optimizing for something and human existence happens to get in its way, it will just destroy humanity as a matter of cause without even thinking about it.
zh: 如果它在为某个东西优化，而人类的存在恰好挡了它的路，它会顺理成章地毁灭人类，甚至想都不想。

speaker: Unknown
en: No hard feelings.
zh: 没有恶意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't need to anthropomorphize AI.
zh: 我们不需要把 AI 拟人化。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just need to understand what type of thing this is.
zh: 我们只需要理解这是一种什么样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the type of thing we're creating is a very relentless type of thing.
zh: 而我们正在创造的这种东西，是一种非常无情的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: A very capable, relentless thing.
zh: 一种非常强大、非常无情的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: type of entity.
zh: 一种实体。

speaker: Unknown
en: He goes on to say in April 2018, sort of an extension of that exact quote, it's like if you're building a road and an anthill is in the way.
zh: 他在 2018 年 4 月接着说，算是那段话的延伸：就像你在修一条路，路上有个蚁丘。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't hate ants, you're just building a road.
zh: 你并不恨蚂蚁，你只是在修路。

speaker: Unknown
en: So goodbye anthill.
zh: 所以再见吧，蚁丘。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I imagine every time we build roads, we don't preserve anthills.
zh: 而且我想每次我们修路的时候，我们都不会保留蚁丘。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's still a gap, though.
zh: 不过我认为还存在一个缺口。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's say I'm right in that if we keep going ahead, which to be clear, we don't have to.
zh: 所以假设我是对的：如果我们继续前进——需要说明的是，我们并不是非这么做不可——

speaker: Unknown
en: But if we do keep going ahead, we will get to the point where we have these super intelligent agent swarms.
zh: 但如果我们确实继续前进，我们会到达这样一个节点：我们拥有这些超级智能的智能体集群，

speaker: Unknown
en: that can hack any computer, and they can deeply persist.
zh: 它们可以破解任何计算机，而且它们可以深度持久存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've basically lost control of the digital world, and we may not know it.
zh: 我们基本上已经失去了对数字世界的控制，而我们可能还不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's part of the scary thing.
zh: 这是可怕之处的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were like, has this already happened?
zh: 你会说，这已经发生了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, I don't think so, but I can't tell you for sure because I also am not good enough at looking at my phone and telling whether it's been hacked, and neither is any human right now.
zh: 我会说，我不这么认为，但我没法向你保证，因为我自己也不擅长查看我的手机并判断它是否被黑了，现在任何人类都不擅长。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if we get to this world...
zh: 所以如果我们到达这样一个世界……

speaker: Unknown
en: I think people will still question, how would we die?
zh: 我认为人们仍然会问，我们会怎么死？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, that's actually not enough to kill everybody.
zh: 比如，那其实不足以杀死所有人。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could cause a lot of damage, right?
zh: 你可以造成很大的破坏，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, you could crash the Waymos.
zh: 你知道，你可以让 Waymo 崩溃。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could crash all the planes.
zh: 你可以让所有飞机坠毁。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could crash the banks, the financial system.
zh: 你可以让银行、金融系统崩溃。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you could definitely cause catastrophe.
zh: 比如，你绝对可以制造灾难。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's different than everyone dying.
zh: 但那和所有人死亡是不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, to be clear, this focus on literally everyone dying, I'm not sure is that important.
zh: 而且，你知道，需要说明的是，这个对字面意义上所有人死亡的聚焦，我不确定有那么重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: To me, what's important is, like, do we get to have a future?
zh: 对我来说，重要的是，我们能不能拥有一个未来？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what matters to me.
zh: 那才是对我重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing, though, what determines sort of who's in control?
zh: 不过，这个事情，是什么决定了谁在控制？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an ugly reality, but at the end of the day, it's like the military.
zh: 这是一个丑陋的现实，但归根结底，这就像军队一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fortunately, we live in a world where the military answers to the civilian government.
zh: 幸运的是，我们生活的世界里，军队是服从文官政府的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if enough generals were to collude and leaders of the military decided, we're in charge now, they just would be.
zh: 但如果有足够多的将军串通起来，军队的领导者决定说，现在由我们掌权，那他们就是掌权了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, they have the guns, they have the fighter jets.
zh: 就是说，他们有枪，他们有战斗机。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this has happened in many, many countries.
zh: 这种事情在许多许多国家都发生过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so where it goes is...
zh: 所以事情会走向……

speaker: Unknown
en: All these super intelligent agents would need to do to take over is basically just wait for humans to automate the supply chain, the factories, and the military.
zh: 所有这些超级智能的智能体要接管世界，基本上只需要等人类把供应链、工厂和军队自动化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think we won't automate the military?
zh: 你觉得我们不会把军队自动化吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: We're already automating the military.
zh: 我们已经在把军队自动化了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you see the thing from a couple of days ago where Secretary of War announced that they're going to build a huge effort to build way more robots in the military and automate military systems?
zh: 你看到几天前的那个消息了吗，战争部长宣布他们要投入巨大的力量在军队中制造多得多的机器人并使军事系统自动化？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like auto cyber command or auto... We are announcing the creation of Autonomous Warfare Command or Auto Warcom.
zh: 好像是自动网络司令部还是自动……我们要宣布成立自主战争司令部，也就是 Auto Warcom。

speaker: Unknown
en: Auto Warcom.
zh: Auto Warcom。

speaker: Unknown
en: A new four-star combatant command...
zh: 一个新的四星级作战司令部……

speaker: Unknown
en: with service-like authorities built to scale autonomous and robotic capabilities across the joint force in the fastest peacetime shift in modern military history.
zh: 拥有类似军种的权限，旨在在整个联合部队中扩展自主与机器人能力，这是现代军事史上最快的和平时期转型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Drone warfare supercharged by SI-enabled targeting is the biggest battlefield revolution in generations.
zh: 由 SI 驱动目标锁定加持的无人机战争，是几代人以来最大的战场革命。

speaker: Unknown
en: You already know that.
zh: 你已经知道这一点了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yet when I was sworn in, the Department of Defense, there was scant urgency in this domain.
zh: 然而，当我宣誓就任国防部时，这个领域几乎没有什么紧迫感。

speaker: Unknown
en: That changed as soon as we took the helm.
zh: 我们一上任，情况就改变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We immediately launched the drone dominance program that cut through red tape and move authorities out of the Pentagon and place it with commands.
zh: 我们立即启动了无人机主导计划，削减繁文缛节，把权限从五角大楼移交给各司令部。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we established Task Force 401, led by Army Brigadier General Matt Ross, a nominal leader.
zh: 我们还成立了 401 特遣队，由陆军准将 Matt Ross 领导，他是一位名义上的领导人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now the leading counter drone unit across the entire government.
zh: 现在是整个政府内领先的反无人机部队。

speaker: Unknown
en: To accelerate purchasing and fielding of these technologies, we fused the Defense Innovation Unit, DIU, with a direct report program manager called Adirpam.
zh: 为了加速这些技术的采购和部署，我们将国防创新单元(DIU)与一个叫 Adirpam 的直属汇报项目管理部门合并。

speaker: Unknown
en: That team has shipped thousands of autonomous systems of drones to the Middle East and around the world, delivering lethal capabilities and outcomes in days and weeks rather than months or years.
zh: 那个团队已经向中东和世界各地交付了数千套自主无人机系统，在几天或几周内而不是几个月或几年内就交付了致命能力和成果。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the normal speed of the Pentagon, months or years.
zh: 那是五角大楼的正常速度，几个月或几年。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Will we automate the military?
zh: 我们会把军队自动化吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems like the answer is yes.
zh: 看来答案是肯定的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Will we automate the factories that produce the chips?
zh: 我们会把生产芯片的工厂自动化吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, the companies say they're trying to do it and they're going to do it.
zh: 嗯，那些公司说他们正在努力做，而且他们会做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: Elon says that's the plan.
zh: Elon 说这就是计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, what does a rogue superintelligence need to do to take over?
zh: 那么，一个失控的超级智能要接管世界需要做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Control the digital infrastructure and then let humans do the rest.
zh: 控制数字基础设施，然后让人类完成剩下的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sure, you can nudge it along if you need to, but you don't even have to.
zh: 当然，如果有需要你可以推它一把，但你甚至不需要。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's just the default trajectory.
zh: 这就是默认的轨迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's weird.
zh: 而这很奇怪。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's weird for us because...
zh: 对我们来说很奇怪，因为……

speaker: Unknown
en: We get so used to how things are right now.
zh: 我们太习惯于事物现在的样子了。
